title: About templates
text: About templates Employees Client admins MSP / reseller admins A few things about how templates behave are worth knowing, whether you're picking one for yourself or curating a list for your company. Who makes templates Templates are designed and maintained by CAD staff. Client admins and MSP admins choose which templates are offered (see Managing templates ), and employees choose among what's offered (see Choosing your template ) — but nobody outside CAD authors or edits a template itself. How a template handles your info Missing fields just disappear. If you don't have a job title or mobile number set, that line doesn't show "Job Title" as a placeholder — it's simply left out, and the layout closes up around it. Text color is chosen for you, to stay readable. You don't pick text color directly: designs updated for this read their own background and use dark text on a light background, white on a dark one; older designs do the same thing based on your brand color instead. Either way, it stays readable. Fonts are fixed per template. Each template uses a small set of fonts chosen by its CAD designer — there's no per-person or per-company font choice today. Long text shrinks, then truncates. A long name or title shrinks to fit first; if it's still too long, it's cut off with an ellipsis rather than overflowing the card. Some designs are see-through, letting the page behind the card show through with a frosted look. Text stays readable, and a printed or e-ink version is always solid. What a specific template looks like (exact spacing, logo size, layout) can change as CAD continues refining templates — this page describes how templates behave in general, not the current look of any one template.

title: Aliases
text: Aliases Employees Client admins An alias is an extra email address on a mailbox — a second domain, or a role-style address — that can get its own CardLink card. For client admins: activating an alias CardLink finds aliases automatically from Microsoft 365 and lists them, but doesn't turn them into cards on its own. In the admin console's Aliases tab, press Activate to give one its own share link and card. Deactivate hides it again (and its link stops resolving). Your company also needs "Include aliases" turned on overall for this tab to have anything to activate. Open the admin console → For employees: what it looks like Once your admin activates an alias for you, it shows up in your portal under My cards alongside your main card, as its own row. You can edit the alias's job title and other allowed fields independently of your main card — it's meant for a different role or brand, so it doesn't have to match. For design, an alias can either pick its own from the gallery, or choose "Use my main card's design" — which keeps following your main card as that changes, rather than locking in a one-time copy. A tick for "Also use this design on my other addresses" on any address applies a pick everywhere at once (skipping anything your admin has locked). The cap on how many designs you can keep counts distinct designs across your main card, aliases, and any claimed mailboxes together — not a separate cap per address. Open the employee portal → Employees can't activate an alias themselves — that's always a client admin action.

title: Analytics
text: Analytics Client admins MSP / reseller admins An Analytics view shows how your cards are actually being used, scoped to your own company (or, for an MSP, every company you manage). What it shows Card views over time, with a daily chart Your most-viewed cards Cards that haven't been opened at all in the period — useful for spotting a card nobody's actually using A breakdown by device and by place (country/city) Employee portal activity — sign-ins, template choices, mailbox claims, and similar self-service actions What it doesn't show No visitor names or email addresses are shown — this is view counts and patterns, not individual visitor tracking. Link previews and bots (the kind of automated request a messaging app makes when generating a link preview) aren't counted by default, so the numbers reflect real opens. Where to find it Client admins see an Analytics tab on their company's page in the admin console. MSP/reseller admins have their own Analytics page covering every client they manage. Tables can be exported to CSV. There's also a separate Activity page: a client admin sees their own company's activity, and an MSP admin sees activity across every company they manage, with the option to narrow to just one. Open the admin console →

title: Employee portal tour
text: Employee portal tour Employees Sign in with your Microsoft work account to reach your portal — one page with everything you can manage yourself. Open the employee portal → Section What it's for My cards One row per address you have — your own card, any active aliases, and any shared mailbox you've claimed. Pick which one is Primary (what shares by default), and edit the fields you're allowed to. See below for how design (template) choice works here. Devices Add a physical NFC card or badge, point it at one of your addresses (the picklist shows the name and address together), label it, and switch a lost one off (or back on). Shared Mailboxes Claim or release a shared mailbox. Once claimed, it gets its own row in My cards, where you pick its design the same way as any other address. Admin Only shown if you're an admin for your company. Grant or revoke admin access for a teammate, and jump into the admin console. Every company must always have at least one admin. My cards, in detail Each row shows a thumbnail of the design that address is currently using, and why: your own pick, matching your main card, your company's default, or set by your admin. Press Share , Make primary , or Edit details right from the row. Press Change design to open a gallery in place, with Company , Seasonal , and Basic filters. A larger preview opens in a pop-up over the page rather than a separate page. On an alias, you can instead choose "Use my main card's design" — it then keeps following your main card's design as that changes, rather than locking in whatever it was at the time. A tick for "Also use this design on my other addresses" applies your pick everywhere at once, skipping any address your admin has locked or where that design isn't offered. If your admin has assigned and locked a design for an address, you'll see "Locked by your admin" there instead of a picker. If your company has turned off design changes entirely, there's no button at all — a note says so. A "Picks used" line reads something like "You have picked 2 of 3 designs allowed" — the cap counts different designs across all your addresses, so the same design on two addresses only counts once. If your company's plan is about to change, an affected row shows "Leaves <date>" ahead of time. Motion Some designs can move — an entrance animation, or an animated/video background (no designs do yet, so this won't change anything you see today, but the switch is live). An "Animate my cards" switch in My cards turns motion off for every address you have at once (an alias follows its main card; a claimed shared mailbox follows whoever's card was actually tapped). Your company can also turn motion off for everyone on a domain, and your own device's reduced-motion setting is respected too — any of these can turn motion off, never back on if a level above has already turned it off. A card with no motion in its design is unaffected either way. If a card's motion loops, a small button in its corner lets a visitor pause and restart it. Signing out of the portal also signs you out of Microsoft in that browser.

title: How your card works
text: How your card works Employees Client admins Every digital card — on a link, a QR code, or a physical NFC card or badge — points at the same live page. Here's what happens when someone taps or scans it. The short version Each card has its own address. Opening it (by tap, scan, or link) always shows that person's current card, pulled fresh from the company directory. If something about your card is wrong — name, title, photo — that's a directory data issue, not a problem with the tap itself; see What's on your card . When a card says "This card is unavailable" This message means the card isn't being shown right now. There are only a few reasons: Reason Who can fix it The link or device was switched off You (in the portal's Devices section, for a lost device) or your admin The person or mailbox is flagged "stale" Your client admin — see Why a card shows "unavailable" The company's account is suspended Your client admin / CardLink support A link that doesn't match any card at all shows a plain "not found" instead. Lost a physical NFC card or badge? You can switch it off yourself from the portal's Devices section — see the employee portal tour . Motion A card whose design moves — and whose motion loops — shows a small translucent button in its lower-right corner that anyone viewing it can use to pause or restart it. See Employee portal tour for how motion gets turned off, by the company, by you, or by your own device.

title: Managing templates
text: Managing templates Client admins As a client admin, you control which templates your company uses, and whether employees get any say. How a card's template is decided CardLink checks these in order and uses the first match: A template you've assigned to that person, alias, or mailbox (optionally locked — see Assignments below), or the one they picked for themselves if you haven't For shared mailboxes only: your domain's "Default for Shared Mailboxes" Your domain's default template The standard CardLink template If a template gets deleted, anything using it just falls through to the next one in this list. An alias with no pick of its own, and no assignment, follows its person's current pick instead — not the domain default — and keeps following it as that changes. What you can set, and where Setting Where Your domain's default template, and the default for shared mailboxes Admin console, Domains tab Whether employees may choose their own template, and how many they can keep Admin console, Self-Service tab Which templates are offered for employees to choose from Admin console, Self-Service tab Which templates are offered for a specific shared mailbox Admin console, Mailboxes tab Assign a specific person's, alias's, or shared mailbox's design directly, and optionally lock it so they can't change it — Studio plan only Admin console, Assignments tab Whether cards animate on this domain (on by default; employees have their own switch too, in My cards) Admin console, Domains tab A template tagged for people only can't be offered for shared mailboxes. Assigning and locking a design On the Studio plan, the Assignments tab lets you give a specific person, alias, or shared mailbox a particular design directly, and optionally lock it. A lock on a person also covers their aliases; a lock on a shared mailbox covers every current claimant. A locked employee sees "Set by your admin" in their portal instead of a picker. Each change can be undone right after you make it. See Template availability & specials for what each plan includes. Open the admin console → See also About templates for how templates handle missing fields, text color, fonts, and long text, and Template availability & specials for why you may only see some templates to choose from.

title: Managing your clients
text: Managing your clients MSP / reseller admins For each client company assigned to you, you can do everything a client admin can do for their own company — no more, no less. What you can change, per client Company name and contact details, allowed domains and the primary domain, brand color, logo, website, and support phone Whether shared mailboxes and aliases are included for that company Self-service template settings: whether employees may choose their own template, the cap on how many they can keep, and which templates are offered Per-domain settings: default template, default for shared mailboxes, stage, colors, and buttons Activating and deactivating aliases Marking mailboxes claimable, and each mailbox's template pool Card overrides, template previews, and triggering a sync (Sync now) See Managing templates and Why a card shows "unavailable" for the details — they apply the same way whether you're a client admin or an MSP admin working inside a client's company. What's off-limits Some things are restricted for every admin, client or MSP, and are CAD-staff only: Seat limits, custom rates, and a client's package details A company's status (active, suspended, archived) Creating, editing, or deleting templates in the shared catalog — you can only choose among what's already there Another MSP's companies, or anything about your own MSP's partner record A plan change (moving a client between Starter/Pro/Studio) isn't on that list — you can start one on a client's behalf from their Plan change tab, same as CAD staff can. It's logged as a support action under your own login, with a reason. See Plans, roles & plan changes for how the change itself works. New clients Setting up a brand-new client company is handled by CAD staff, including assigning it to your MSP. Once a company exists and is assigned to you, you take it from there using everything above. There's no self-service way to add a new client yet. Open the admin console →

title: MSP/reseller admin overview
text: MSP/reseller admin overview MSP / reseller admins If you manage CardLink for more than one client company, you're an MSP (reseller) admin. Your experience is similar to a single client admin's, but built around managing several companies from one account. Open the admin console → Where you land after signing in One sign-in covers every client company you've been assigned. You land on My Clients — a list of only your own companies — and open one by clicking it. From there you see the same company page a single client admin sees for their own company: Overview, Domains, Cards, Aliases, Mailboxes, Self-Service, Overrides, Devices, and Settings tabs. There's no client-switcher dropdown inside a company — to move to a different client, go back to My Clients and pick another. Your menu Your side menu has four items: My Clients , My Team , Changelog , and Settings . A single client admin sees "My Company" in place of the client list, and doesn't have a team page. What's not in your view Dashboard, Partners, Leads, Reports, the template authoring area, Transactions, and System pages are all CAD-staff only — you won't see them. For what you can actually change within each client company, see Managing your clients . For managing your own team, see Your team .

title: Signing in as an MSP admin
text: Signing in as an MSP admin MSP / reseller admins MSP admin sign-in is different from a client admin's — it doesn't use Microsoft sign-in. Getting started You'll receive an invitation link, either from CAD staff or from a teammate who's already an MSP admin for your company. Opening it lets you set a password and scan a QR code to set up an authenticator app. Every time after that Sign in with your email, your password, and the current six-digit code from your authenticator app. One account covers every client company you've been assigned — there's no separate authorization step per client. Open the admin console → If CAD suspends your MSP, none of your team can sign in until it's reinstated. Managing your teammates' access is covered in Your team .

title: Your team
text: Your team MSP / reseller admins The My Team page is where you manage who else at your MSP has admin access. What you can do Invite a new teammate (they'll get the same invitation link, password, and authenticator setup described in Signing in as an MSP admin ) Disable a teammate's access, or re-enable it You only see your own MSP's team — not any other MSP's. Open the admin console →

title: Photo and logo guidance
text: Photo and logo guidance Employees Client admins Your card's images come from two different places. Getting the format and size right at the source means your card loads faster and looks sharp, since CardLink displays what it's given rather than re-processing it. Your profile photo Your card uses your Microsoft 365 / Entra profile photo — whatever's set there reaches your card at the next sync. Your card displays it at 360×360 pixels, so: Use a JPEG, not a PNG or HEIC. A photo at the same visual quality is dramatically smaller as a JPEG than as a PNG — a typical PNG photo can be 5-10x larger than an equivalent JPEG for no visible difference on a card this size. Square (1:1 crop), head and shoulders. Matches how it's displayed — anything else gets cropped to fit. Around 360–500 px on a side is plenty. Larger just means a bigger download for no visible gain, since the card never shows it larger than 360×360. If an uploaded photo is unusually large, it may display smaller than expected rather than failing outright — keeping it JPEG and reasonably sized avoids that entirely. Your company logo Client admins Set in your company's CardLink settings, not from an individual profile. A few things to know: PNG with a transparent background if your logo needs to sit on a colored card background; JPEG is fine for a logo that's always on white. Keep the file size modest — a logo doesn't need to be print-resolution to look sharp at card size. If your logo looks cropped or cut off (common with a wide logo or one that includes a wordmark), your admin console's Domains tab has a logo shape and fit setting that can fix this per domain — worth checking before trying to resize the logo file itself. Open the admin console → Social links and brand colors Client admins From the admin console's Domains tab , you can set up to 8 social links (each pointing to the platform's own site) that show as a row of icons on a card, and your domain's Secondary and Accent brand colors (alongside your existing Primary brand color) for templates that use them. These also carry over to Save to Contacts. Open the admin console → Template backgrounds If you're working with CAD on a custom template background, that's handled directly with your designer — it's a different asset path from your photo or logo and isn't self-service today.

title: Plans, roles & plan changes
text: Plans, roles & plan changes Client admins MSP / reseller admins Your company's plan decides which template-management controls you get. Two admin roles split who can do what. On your company's page in the admin console, Assignments, Plan change, and Roles each have their own tab, grouped with the rest of your company's settings in the menu down the left. Plans Starter, Pro, and Studio decide which design-management controls your company gets — never what an individual card is allowed to show. See Template availability & specials for the full breakdown of what each plan includes. Roles Within your company, three roles split admin responsibilities: Super admin — administers the company day to day, but cannot touch billing. Billing admin — handles billing and plan changes, but has no other admin rights. Admin — handles day-to-day design work. One person can hold more than one role at once, and your company always keeps at least one Super admin, one Billing admin, and one Admin. A Super admin adds or removes a company admin from the console's Roles tab (CardLink or your MSP/reseller can also do this on your behalf, as a logged support action). A new admin starts out as a plain Admin — an existing Billing admin has to separately hand over the Billing role. Removing someone ends any session they already have open right away. Changing your plan A Billing admin or Super admin starts a plan change from the admin console's Plan change tab (CardLink or your MSP/reseller can also do this on your behalf, as a logged support action). Moving up a plan is immediate. Moving down is never instant — you get a 4–7 day notice (or it takes effect at your next invoice date, whichever applies). In that window, you review which designs the new plan no longer allows and pick replacements. Your company's default design must be replaced; anything else is optional. Only the designs the new plan drops stop applying — nothing else changes, and nothing is deleted. Notices about an upcoming plan change show up in the console and portal itself (the "Leaves <date>" labels you'll see on affected cards) — don't expect a separate email about it yet. Starting a plan change here updates which designs are available; it doesn't yet update what you're billed — that's still handled separately for now. Open the admin console →

title: Shared mailboxes
text: Shared mailboxes Employees Client admins A shared mailbox (like info@ or sales@) can have its own CardLink card that one or more employees claim and use. For client admins: making a mailbox claimable In the admin console's Mailboxes tab, mark specific shared mailboxes as claimable. The mailbox needs to be a current, non-stale card for this to work — the console will warn you if a mailbox you've marked claimable can't actually be claimed yet. You can also set a display name for a shared mailbox's card from the Overrides section — unlike a personal card, a shared mailbox's name can be overridden, since there's no single person's identity to protect. It takes effect at the next sync. Open the admin console → For employees: claiming and releasing In the portal's Shared Mailboxes section, press Claim on any mailbox your admin has made available (you can give it an optional display name). You'll get your own share link and card for it, and it shows up as its own row in My cards , where you pick its design the same way as any other address. Several people can claim the same mailbox at once, each with their own separate link and their own design pick. Press Release to switch your link off. Claiming it again later reuses the same link rather than creating a new one. Open the employee portal → One thing to know Because several people can claim the same mailbox, everyone who claims it shares one underlying record — so you can't change the mailbox's name or title from the portal, only pick which design it uses for your own link.

title: Signing in to the admin console
text: Signing in to the admin console Client admins The admin console uses your normal Microsoft work account, plus one extra step. Open the admin console → Who can get in Only people your company has authorized as admins. Your company's contact person is the first admin by default; they can grant admin access to teammates from the portal's Admin section. What signing in looks like Choose Sign in with Microsoft and sign in with your normal work account. Enter a six-digit code from an authenticator app. The first time, you'll scan a QR code to set this up; after that, you'll enter the current code from your app every time you sign in. This second step happens on every sign-in, even if your company already requires Microsoft multi-factor authentication — it's a separate check specific to the admin console. Signing out also signs you out of Microsoft in that browser.

title: Template availability and specials
text: Template availability and specials Client admins MSP / reseller admins Not every template is available to every company — and some are only around for a limited time. What you'll see In the admin console, you'll only see templates that have actually been made available to your company. Some are available all the time; others are seasonal specials with a note on how long they're around. When a special's window closes, it quietly drops out of what you (or your employees) can newly pick — no error, it just stops being offered. A card already using a special keeps it If an employee picked a seasonal template before it expired, their card keeps using it — expiry only affects new choices, never a card that's already set. What employees see Employees only ever choose from what you've offered them (see Managing templates ) — and that list automatically reflects availability, so you don't have to manually remove something that's expired. Your plan also decides what's available Your company's plan gates both the design catalog and the controls you get: Plan Design catalog Controls Starter Core designs only No employee picks — you set the design for the whole company Pro Core, plus CardLink and community designs Adds employee self-service picks Studio Everything in Pro, plus designs CardLink builds for your company specifically Adds the Assignments tab — assign and optionally lock a design per person, alias, or shared mailbox See Plans, roles & plan changes for how a plan change itself works. Open the admin console →

title: Why a card shows "unavailable"
text: Why a card shows "unavailable" Client admins CardLink checks every card once a day (and whenever you press "Sync now"). If a card no longer qualifies, it's marked stale and shows as unavailable until the cause is fixed and it syncs again. When this runs Automatically once a day, early morning. You can also trigger it on demand from your company's overview page in the admin console with Sync now — useful right after you've fixed something and don't want to wait. Every stale reason, plain language What you'll see What it means How to fix it Not in the directory The account was deleted, or is no longer a member Restore the account in Microsoft 365, or remove the card if it's gone for good No email address The account has no email set Add an email address in Microsoft 365 Account disabled The account is disabled in Microsoft 365 Re-enable it Shared mailboxes turned off Your company has shared-mailbox cards disabled Turn them back on in the admin console Domain not allowed The account's email domain isn't in your Allowed Domains list Add the domain in the admin console's settings Alias not active The alias was deactivated, aliases are off, or its domain isn't allowed Reactivate the alias, turn aliases on, or allow its domain Not returned by the last sync Catch-all for anything else the directory didn't return Check the account in Microsoft 365; sync again After you fix it Press Sync now rather than waiting for the next automatic run — a stale flag clears the moment a sync finds the cause resolved. This is reversible both ways: a card can go stale and come back as many times as the underlying cause changes. Employees and portal users can't fix a stale card themselves — this always needs a client admin to resolve the underlying Microsoft 365 or CardLink setting. Removing a card for good If a stale card should be removed permanently rather than fixed (someone has left the company, for example), your admin console has a Purge action for that. Open the admin console →

title: What's on your card
text: What's on your card Employees Your card pulls most of its information straight from your company's Microsoft 365 directory, refreshed once a day. From the directory (not editable by you) Display name, first and last name, job title, department, email, office phone, mobile phone, office location, and your profile photo all come from Microsoft 365. The directory always wins: if your IT admin updates one of these in Microsoft 365, your card updates at the next sync. You cannot override your name on your personal card — that's intentional, so nobody can impersonate someone else. What you (or your admin) can fill in If the directory doesn't have a value for mobile phone, office location, or job title, you — or your client admin — can fill that one in yourself. The moment the directory does have a value, it takes over again. From your company (not from you) Your company name, website, logo, and brand colors come from your company's CardLink settings, not from your individual profile. Your photo Your card uses your Microsoft 365 / Entra profile photo. If you need to update it, change it the same way you'd change it anywhere else tied to your Microsoft account — it will reach your card at the next sync. What's in Save to Contacts Saving your card to someone's contacts carries your name, title, department, office location, phone and email, a link back to your CardLink card, your company's social profiles (if your admin has set any up — see Photo and logo guidance ), and your photo. (How it displays depends on the phone it's saved to.) To fill in a gap the directory doesn't have, or see what's on your card now: Open the employee portal →

title: Choosing your template
text: Choosing your template Employees Your card's look — its template, which the portal calls a "design" — can be changed from the portal, if your company allows it. Where to change it Sign in to the portal and open My cards . Find the row for the address you want to change, and press Change design . A gallery opens in place, filterable by Company, Seasonal, or Basic, each with a live preview of your own card in that design. Open the employee portal → Why you might not see a choice Design choice is set per company. Your client admin controls whether employees can choose at all, how many designs are offered, and a cap on how many you can keep across all your addresses (picking the same design on two addresses only counts once toward that cap). If you don't see a choice, one of a few things may be true: your company has turned design changes off entirely, or your admin has assigned and locked a specific design for that address — in which case you'll see "Locked by your admin" instead of a picker. Either way, your card still has a design; your admin just picked it. Aliases and shared mailboxes An alias has its own row in My cards and its own design choice, including an option to just follow your main card's design instead of picking separately — see Aliases . A claimed shared mailbox also gets its own row — see Shared mailboxes . See also About templates for how templates handle missing fields, text color, fonts, and long text.
